hints: Compute the running cumulative frequencies for the four intervals: 14, 62, 132, 140.
Identify the upper boundaries of each interval: 50, 80, 100, 120.
Plot points at (40, 0), (50, 14), (80, 62), (100, 132), (120, 140) and join with a smooth curve or polygon.
walkthrough:
Calculate the upper class boundaries and running cumulative frequencies:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Circumference (cm)} & \text{Upper Boundary} & \text{Frequency} & \text{Cumulative Frequency} \\ \hline 40 < c \le 50 & 50 & 14 & 14 \\ 50 < c \le 80 & 80 & 48 & 14 + 48 = 62 \\ 80 < c \le 100 & 100 & 70 & 62 + 70 = 132 \\ 100 < c \le 120 & 120 & 8 & 132 + 8 = 140 \\ \hline\end{array}$$
Connect the points with an increasing curve or polygon.

ai_rubric.Constructing Cumulative-Frequency Graphs: Plots (50, 14), (80, 62), (100, 132), (120, 140) on linear axes and connects them.

teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Construct the cumulative frequency table.
For continuous data given in inequality intervals $a < c \le b$, cumulative frequencies are plotted strictly at the upper boundary $b$:
- At $c = 40$: $\text{CF} = 0$
- At $c = 50$: $\text{CF} = 14$
- At $c = 80$: $\text{CF} = 14 + 48 = 62$
- At $c = 100$: $\text{CF} = 62 + 70 = 132$
- At $c = 120$: $\text{CF} = 132 + 8 = 140$

Step 2: Plot the points on the grid:
$$(40, 0), \quad (50, 14), \quad (80, 62), \quad (100, 132), \quad (120, 140)$$
Step 3: Connect the points with an increasing curve or straight-line segments (cumulative frequency polygon).

hints: Read the cumulative frequency corresponding to circumference $c = 75$ cm from your graph (or use linear interpolation in the 50 to 80 interval).
Subtract this value from the total number of trees (140) to find the number with circumference greater than 75 cm.
Divide by 140 and multiply by 100% to find the percentage.
walkthrough:
Read the cumulative frequency at $c = 75$ cm from the graph:
$$\text{Number of trees with } c \le 75 \approx 54 \quad \left(\text{or by linear interpolation: } 14 + \frac{25}{30} \times 48 = 54\right)$$

Calculate the number of trees with circumference greater than $75$ cm:
$$\text{Number of trees with } c > 75 = 140 - 54 = 86$$

Calculate the percentage of the total $140$ trees:
$$\text{Percentage} = \frac{86}{140} \times 100\% \approx 61.4\% \quad (\text{acceptable range: } 60.5\% \le \text{Ans} \le 64.5\%)$$Lancashire

ai_rubric.Reading Cumulative-Frequency Graphs: Reads CF around 54 at c = 75, subtracts from 140 to get 86, and calculates percentage 61.4% (60.5% to 64.5%).

teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Determine the number of trees with circumference up to $75$ cm.
Locate $75$ on the horizontal circumference axis and read the corresponding value on the vertical cumulative frequency axis:
$$\text{CF}(75) \approx 54$$
(By linear interpolation between $(50, 14)$ and $(80, 62)$: the fraction of the interval from $50$ to $75$ is $\frac{75 - 50}{80 - 50} = \frac{25}{30} = \frac{5}{6}$. Then $14 + \frac{5}{6} \times 48 = 14 + 40 = 54$).

Step 2: Find the number of trees with circumference larger than $75$ cm:
$$\text{Count} = 140 - 54 = 86$$

Step 3: Convert to a percentage of the total sample size $140$:
$$\text{Percentage} = \frac{86}{140} \times 100\% = \frac{43}{70} \times 100\% \approx 61.4286\% \approx 61.4\%$$
Any reading yielding an answer between $60.5\%$ and $64.5\%$ is fully credited.
